title: Set 254

sentences.ko: 이사를 갈지 말지 계속 왔다 갔다 해. 새 집이 회사에서 훨씬 가까워서 매일 한 시간 정도는 더 생기는데, 월세가 한 달에 200달러 더 비싸거든. 그 한 시간이 나한테 정말 그만한 가치가 있는지 잘 모르겠어.
sentences.text: I keep going back and forth on moving. The new place is way closer to work, so I'd get like an extra hour back every day, but it's two hundred more a month, and I'm not sure that hour is really worth it to me.

alts.text: Can't decide if I should move. New place is way closer to work, I'd get like an hour back every day. But it's two hundred more a month and I dunno if that hour's worth it to me.

I have been unable to decide whether to move. The new apartment is much closer to my office, so I would gain roughly an extra hour each day, but it costs two hundred more per month, and I am not certain that the hour is worth it to me.

sentences.note: **go back and forth** 는 마음을 못 정하고 이랬다저랬다 한다는 뜻이에요. **get like an extra hour back** 의 get ... back 은 잃던 시간을 되찾는다는 말이에요.

sentences.ko: 설탕 안 먹고 2주를 버텼거든. 그런데 회사 동료가 도넛을 사 온 거야. 반 개만 먹자고 다짐했는데 결국 세 개를 먹었어. 문제는 설탕 대신 먹는 음식이 맛이 없다는 거 같아. 그래서 맛있는 게 눈앞에 나타나기만 하면 바로 넘어가 버려.
sentences.text: So I made it two weeks with no sugar, and then my coworker brought in donuts. I told myself I'd only have half of one, but I ended up eating three. I think the problem is I don't even like what I'm eating instead, so the second something good shows up, I just give in.

alts.text: Two weeks, no sugar, then my coworker shows up with donuts. Said I'd just have half of one. Had three. Thing is, I don't even like the stuff I'm eating instead, so the second something good's around, I cave.

I managed two weeks without sugar, and then a colleague brought in donuts. I told myself I would have only half of one, but I ended up eating three. I believe the problem is that I do not even enjoy the food I am eating instead, so as soon as something good appears, I give in.

sentences.note: **made it two weeks** 는 2주를 버텨 냈다는 뜻이에요. **give in** 은 유혹에 지고 만다는 말이고, 캐주얼하게는 **cave** 라고도 해요.

sentences.ko: 잠깐, 내가 지난번에 봤을 때 너 곧 출산이었잖아! 그럼 딸은 이제 몇 개월이야? 그리고 너희 부부 이제 잠은 좀 자? 아니면 아직도 잠은 꿈같은 얘기야?
sentences.text: Wait, last time I saw you, you were about to have the baby! So how old is she now? And are you guys actually sleeping yet, or is that still a joke?

alts.text: Hold on, you were about to have the baby last time I saw you! How old's she now? You guys sleeping yet, or is that still a joke?
The last time we met, you were about to have your baby! How old is she now? And are you and your partner getting any sleep yet, or is that still a distant dream?

sentences.note: **about to have the baby** 는 곧 아기를 낳을 참이라는 뜻이에요. **still a joke** 는 아직도 웃음밖에 안 나올 만큼 어림없는 얘기라는 뜻이에요.

sentences.ko: 진짜로, 몇 년째 똑같이 자르는 머리가 이제 40달러야. 예전엔 25달러였는데 딱히 다르게 해 주는 것도 없잖아. 그래서 그냥 머리를 길러 볼까 생각 중이야.
sentences.text: I swear, the same haircut I've been getting for years is forty dollars now. It used to be twenty-five, and it's not like they're doing anything different, so I'm kind of thinking about just growing it out.

alts.text: Swear to God, my same old haircut's forty bucks now. Used to be twenty-five, and they're not doing anything different, so I'm kinda thinking I'll just grow it out.
Honestly, the same haircut I have had for years now costs forty dollars. It used to cost twenty-five, and they are not doing anything differently, so I am considering simply letting it grow out.

sentences.note: **I swear** 는 진짜라니까 하고 말에 힘을 주는 표현이에요. **grow it out** 은 자르지 않고 머리를 기른다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.ko: 미안, 미안, 오늘 아침에 지하철이 엉망이었어. 역 앞에서 15분쯤 세워 놓고는 아무도 이유를 안 알려 주더라. 그래서 언제 도착할지 말해 줄 수도 없었어.
sentences.text: Sorry, sorry, the train was a mess this morning. They stopped us outside the station for like fifteen minutes and nobody told us why, so I couldn't even tell you when I'd get here.

alts.text: Ugh, my bad! Train was a disaster. We sat outside the station like fifteen minutes, nobody said why, so I couldn't even say when I'd be here.

I apologize for being late. The train was badly disrupted this morning. We were held outside the station for about fifteen minutes without any explanation, so I was unable to let you know when I would arrive.

sentences.note: **a mess** 는 엉망진창이라는 뜻으로, 교통이나 상황이 꼬였을 때 자주 써요. **for like fifteen minutes** 의 like 는 대충, 한 정도라는 뜻이에요.

reviewed: 1번 note 의 get an hour back 은 문장에 그대로 나오지 않아(사이에 like an extra 가 끼어 있음) 실제 문장에 있는 get like an extra hour back 으로 감쌌음
3번 formal 의 out of the question 은 불가능하다는 뜻이라 still a joke(웃음밖에 안 나오는 얘기)와 결이 달라 a distant dream 으로 바꿈
5번 text 의 couldn't even text you when I'd get here 는 도착하면 문자를 보낸다는 뜻으로도 읽혀서 tell you when I'd get here 로 고치고 casual과 한국어도 맞춤
5번 casual 이 text 와 앞부분(Sorry, sorry, train was)이 거의 같아서 첫머리를 바꿈
